texts.preamble: Manjunatha.B.R vs Suhil Ahamad on 16 May, 2025 Kabc020239232021 Appasab Digitally signed by Appasab Ramappa Naik Ramappa Date: 2025.06.03 17:40:21 Naik +0530 Before The Court Of Xxiv Additional Small Causes Judge And The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal And Acjm (Scch-26) At Bengaluru Dated This The 16th Day Of May 2025 Present : Sri. Appasab Naik, B.A.L.L.B.(Spl) Xxiv Addl. Scj & Acjm & Member - Mact Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.4024 Of 2021 Petitioners: 1. Manjunath.B.R., S/o.Rangegowda, Aged about 35 years, R/at No.17, Pleginamma Devasthana Hattira, Kadur Taluk, Kadur, Chikkamagaluru - 577548. Petitioner was died on 29.04.2024 Hence represented by his LR's 1.Pet.(a).Smt.Thulasi.P., W/o.
texts.facts: This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries caused in a Road Traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under: It is the case of the petitioners that, on 08-04-2021 at about 9.00 p.m., while petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-18-EB-4998 to go to Manjunatha.B.R vs Suhil Ahamad on 16 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103681222/ 2 KSRTC Bus Stop at Kanaka Circle, when he reached Opp. Basaveswara Hospital, K.M.Road, Kadur Town, at that time a Bollero Pickup Bearing No.KA-24-8741 came from Opposite side with high speed in rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed against his motor cycle. Due to impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Kadur, wherein he took first aid and then shifted to Shivamogga Govt. Hospital and then shifted to Digvijaya Hospital, Banashankari, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for about 12 days, surgery was conducted, rod was inserted, X-rays were done and advised to take followup treatment. The petitioner has spent more than Rs.6,00,000/- towards conveyance, food nourishment, medical and attendant charges. 3. It is the case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident he was working as bakery cake maker in Maruthi Bakery Kadur and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to the accident he lost his income and future prospects and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to this accident he has lost the income and future prospective life, happiness and earning capacity and has become disabled and dependant. 4. The Kadur Police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the Bollero Pickup bearing Reg.No.KA- 24-8741 in Cr.No.80/2021 under Section 279 & 337 of IPC R/w Sec.187 of MV Act. The accident was occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the 1 st respondent. The policy was valid and was in force at the time of accident. The driver of the said Bollero vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence. The Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents. 5. After service of summons, both the respondents appeared through their counsel. The respondent No.1 has not chosen to file the written statement. The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the averments made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-24-8741 as on the date of alleged accident. It has not issued any policy for the said vehicle covering the date of accident. Hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and the petition against this respondent is liable to be dismissed. on 16 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103681222/ 3 accident i.e., public placed and the same was used without having valid permit in violation of the policy condition and also the MV Act. This respondent seeks protection under Sec. 147, 149 and also under sec.134 of MV Act. It is the mandatory duty of the owner of the vehicle to furnish the particulars of the policy, date, time and place of accident, particulars of injured and the name of the driver etc., but the owner of the vehicle has filed to comply with the statutory demand. As per Sec.158 (6) of M.V Act 1988 it is the mandatory duty of the concerned PS to forward all the relevant documents to the concerned insurer within 30 days from the date of information but the Kadur Police have failed to forward the documents and complied with the statutory demand. The petitioner was not wearing safety head gear at the time of accident and hence there is violation of breach of terms and conditions of the policy. It has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner. It has denied the injuries sustained and amount spent towards the medical expenses. B.N is examined as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.P.14 & 15 and closed his side evidence. On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced their rebuttal evidence and respondent evidence is taken as Nil. 8. The case is posted for arguments, at this stage, Unfortunately, the petitioner expired on 29-04-2024 i.e., during the pendency of the petition. Hence his Legal representative was brought on record as petitioner vide orders dated 27-02-2025. In order to prove the actionable negligence, petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1.
texts.arguments: It is further contended that if the claimant has furnished any policy particulars then this respondent may be permitted to file additional written statement. The person driving the vehicle has "no relation in force" as on the date of accident to drive the vehicle. The driver of the vehicle has not valid and effective driving license to drive the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-24-8741 at the time of accident. It has further contended that the owner of the vehicle knowingly allowed the driver to drive the said vehicle without valid and effective driving license and there is violation of the policy conditions by the owner of the insured vehicle. The insured vehicle was not having FC to ply the vehicle in a place of Manjunatha. B.R vs Suhil Ahamad The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exaggerated one. During pendency of the petition, the petitioner cum injured - Sri.Manjunath.B.R died and his legal representatives were brought on record. The main contention of the second respondent that, as per medical records like wound certificate it is very clear that the injuries sustained by petitioner is simple in nature and there is no grievous injuries and there is no nexus between injuries and death. Moreover, the Postmortem examination of the deceased has not been conducted to find out the cause of his death and no evidence is place on record to prove that the deceased died on account of injuries sustained in the accident. 17. In the absence of such proof, as per the ratio laid down in the decision reported in 2010 KAR MAC 557 between Somavva & others V/s Vijaya Kumar and others, the legal representatives of the deceased are entitled to claim only expenses spent towards the treatment of the deceased petitioner and the loss of income suffered by the deceased during laid-up/treatment period.
